findings.title: Device-limit denial is cached, so a retry bypasses the limit
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device key into localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. When the store rejects a new device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, that key stays cached for the default 29 minutes and the error is returned only for the current call. Authenticate treats that error as a hard failure, but the next anonymous request for the same X-Grafana-Device-Id hits the cache, returns nil, and is issued an anonymous identity without ever being inserted or counted. Refreshing once therefore bypasses the configured device limit, and those sessions never appear in the 30-day count, so the cap stays artificially low. Clear the cache entry (or set it only after a successful write) when tagging fails.

findings.title: Device limit check is not atomic with insert
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active rows and, only if count < deviceLimit, runs a separate INSERT. Those steps are not in one transaction and take no lock, so concurrent anonymous logins can all observe the same count below the cap and all insert. The configured limit can be exceeded under parallel traffic (multiple Grafana instances make this worse). Enforce the cap in the same transaction as the insert, or with a row/advisory lock, so the count and write cannot race.

findings.title: Wire provider signature changed but generated injector was not updated
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts anonstore.AnonStore and now requires db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a deviceLimit argument. Grafana constructs this service from the checked-in Wire injector (pkg/server/wire_gen.go), which is not in this PR. The existing injector still calls the old signature, so the OSS server package will not compile until wire is regenerated and any other call sites are updated.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is undocumented
findings.body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from [auth.anonymous] device_limit (default 0 = unlimited) but this PR does not add the key to conf/defaults.ini or the auth configuration docs. Operators have no documented name, default, or meaning for the limit, so the feature cannot be configured from the shipped sample config.
